comparators.title: A dynamic control-oriented model of climate and crop growth in vertical farms
comparators.authors: Author list as published; DOI source record
comparators.system_domain: Commercial vertical farm lettuce; single-compartment to small-scale VF datasets
comparators.method_summary: Interpretable mechanistic control-oriented ODE model coupling temperature, humidity, CO2, airspeed, lighting inputs (intensity, photoperiod, spectrum), crop dry weight, photosynthesis, respiration, transpiration, LED energy and AC energy. Evaluated against seven independent experimental datasets.

reported_metrics.basis: Reported across model evaluation; source-specific aggregation
reported_metrics.notes: Do not compare directly with NRMSE, CV(RMSE), or unnormalized RMSE from other studies.

reported_metrics.basis: Scenario outcomes under stated treatments and efficiency assumptions

limitations: Uses a perfectly mixed tank assumption for the vertical-farm chamber; does not resolve rack/layer spatial gradients.
Uses a constant AC coefficient of performance; part-load and within-cycle sensible/latent COP variation are not resolved.
The paper itself notes sensitivity of AC energy and lighting-to-AC ratio to the assumed COP.
Commercial and small-scale VF lettuce cases do not establish transfer to underground rock boundaries, groundwater, or cavern infiltration.
comparators.transferability: Strong dynamic crop-climate control comparator and a candidate reduced-order baseline. Pair with spatial CFD and measured zone-level data; do not treat as a complete cavern model.

comparators.title: CFD-based evaluation of air distribution strategies for improving environmental uniformity and reducing energy use in container and building vertical farms
comparators.authors: Author list as published; DOI source record
comparators.system_domain: Container VF 27 m², three layers; building VF 162 m², six layers; mature lettuce LAI=3
comparators.method_summary: Compares ten air-distribution configurations combining direct AC discharge or ducts with rack/aisle fans. Uses validated SST k-omega CFD and evaluates both facility-wide and crop-layer airflow/temperature uniformity.

reported_metrics.basis: CFD validation against field velocity measurements
reported_metrics.notes: Metric is large and should be retained as a model limitation, not hidden by the temperature result.

reported_metrics.basis: CFD validation against field temperature measurements
Container farm simulation; direct AC discharge configuration
Modelled Centre+z sidewall fan configuration vs study baseline
Modelled Centre+z sidewall fan configuration vs study baseline

limitations: Fan-energy reduction is a simulation result, not a measured in-facility electricity saving.
The 34.33% velocity NRMSE is material; airflow claims must retain uncertainty and sampling geometry.
Geometry, LAI, supply arrangement, boundary conditions and validation sensors are specific to the two study facilities.
A velocity-field fit does not establish humidity, condensation, crop physiology, or full-facility HVAC performance.
comparators.transferability: Strong spatial airflow design comparator. Re-run with matched geometry, crop drag, sensor locations, operating points, mesh study and an independently frozen validation set.

comparators.title: Experimental analysis of temperature uniformity in a vertical smart-farm with radiant cooling panels
comparators.venue: International Journal of Air-Conditioning and Refrigeration, Volume 34, article 6
comparators.system_domain: Lettuce vertical-smart-farm mock-up with ceiling and cultivation-bed radiant cooling panels
comparators.method_summary: One-minute temperature logging at multiple horizontal and vertical locations; 1 h LED-off and 2 h LED-on windows. The experiment tests spatial temperature uniformity, not a full HVAC/dehumidification energy balance.

reported_metrics.basis: Comparison with prior convection-only study results, not a concurrent randomized HVAC trial

limitations: Cooling capacity was assumed sufficient; the test was not a cooling-capacity or energy-efficiency comparison.
A dehumidifier was installed but not operated; condensation control was not demonstrated.
Short LED-off / LED-on observation windows do not establish seasonal dynamics or long-duration stability.
The authors report a middle-layer location with local deviations exceeding 2 K during much of the LED-on observation; aggregate uniformity can conceal local excursions.
comparators.transferability: Useful experimental comparator for spatial temperature uniformity and radiant-panel layout. Not a dehumidification, condensation, thermal-storage or cavern heat-rejection qualification.

comparators.title: A transient energy-agriculture model to predict energy footprint of vertical farms
comparators.authors: F. Ceccanti, G. Di Lorenzo, A. Bischi, L. Incrocci, A. Pardossi and A. Baccioli
comparators.venue: Energy Conversion and Management, Volume 332, article 119740
comparators.system_domain: Vertical farm model in a humid continental climate; annual scenario simulations
comparators.method_summary: Five-minute-step lumped-parameter model with dynamic leaf-area index, crop growth, transpiration, envelope, lighting, heating/cooling, humidification/dehumidification, heat pumps/chillers, cleaning and CO2 fertilization. COP varies with external conditions and part-load factor.

reported_metrics.unit: accuracy improvement as reported by abstract/institutional record
reported_metrics.basis: Variable-COP approach vs compared constant-COP approach
reported_metrics.notes: Publisher highlights also phrase a 40% cooling-energy reduction vs constant COP=3; do not treat that highlight as a measured facility saving or universal reduction.

reported_metrics.unit: accuracy improvement as reported by abstract/institutional record
reported_metrics.basis: Variable-COP approach vs compared constant-COP approach
Most energy-effective of nine simulated indoor growing conditions

reported_metrics.unit: g fresh mass L^-1 recovered water

limitations: Modelled scenarios, not a field demonstration of the stated cooling or water recovery gains.
System and climate assumptions are study-specific; energy-food ratios are not directly comparable without matching crop, facility boundary and functional unit.
The reported 40% wording differs between publisher highlights and abstract/institutional record; prefer the more precise accuracy-improvement wording pending source-method audit.
comparators.transferability: Strong transient whole-process comparator for variable-COP, dynamic LAI and moisture-flow coupling. Use as a model-structure comparison, not a claimed 40% energy-saving target.

comparators.title: Energy optimization of a vertical farm in a Canadian hemiboreal humid climate
comparators.venue: Sustainable Energy Technologies and Assessments, Volume 89, article 104987
comparators.system_domain: Existing indoor hydroponic vertical farm in Timmins, Ontario, Canada
comparators.method_summary: TRNSYS model checked against facility environmental conditions, equipment runtime and monthly utility billing records; then evaluates outdoor ventilation and air-to-air heat exchanger alternatives under different electricity and CO2 costs.

reported_metrics.basis: Model predictions vs monthly energy billing
Model predictions vs monthly energy billing
Model predictions vs monthly energy billing
Model predictions vs monthly energy billing

reported_metrics.unit: MJ per monthly average day as reported

limitations: Monthly utility billing validation does not by itself validate minute-scale zone climate, canopy microclimate or transient condensation.
Economic ranking of ventilation vs heat exchanger is sensitive to electricity and CO2 prices; halving CO2 price changes the preferred option.
Timmins climate, facility configuration and operating costs do not transfer directly to Johannesburg or an underground site.
comparators.transferability: Useful operational energy-model validation comparator and cost sensitivity study. Match the time aggregation and boundary before comparing errors or savings.

comparators.title: Prediction of Energy Consumption and Energy Savings in an Urban Vertical Farm Benchmark
comparators.authors: Simeng Xie, Pedro Martinez-Vazquez and Charalampos Baniotopoulos
comparators.venue: Energy Science & Engineering, Volume 14, Issue 3, pages 1086–1099
comparators.system_domain: 20-floor, mixed-use Birmingham urban vertical-farm building including cultivation, offices, storage, warehousing and support zones
comparators.method_summary: EnergyPlus model with multiple thermal zones and whole-building / planting / office energy use. Provides a building-scope energy breakdown and simulated design package comparisons.

reported_metrics.unit: % of total building energy in abstract
% of total building energy in abstract

limitations: Mixed-use building boundary includes non-growing functions; whole-building energy share is not a crop-room HVAC share.
The paper reports multiple aggregate EUI figures under different site/source and scope definitions; values must be traced to numerator, denominator and zone boundary before reuse.
The ~20% design package result is simulated and not a measured farm retrofit outcome.
Building-specific weather, solar exposure, envelope and office loads do not transfer to an underground facility.
comparators.transferability: Use to remind the benchmark to separate site/source EUI and cultivation/office/support zones. Not a direct CEA crop-zone comparator.

interpretation_rules: Preserve the original error metric and denominator: RMSE, rRMSE, NRMSE, CV(RMSE), MAPE and NMBE are not interchangeable.
Distinguish measured sensor observations, model-validation metrics, model predictions, simulated design comparisons and author-reported conclusions.
Do not compare kWh per square metre with kWh per kilogram unless crop output, facility area, time window and system boundary are all available.
Do not interpret fan-energy, COP or energy-food scenario results as measured savings unless the physical system was metered in a matched intervention.
A well-mixed climate model cannot be used to claim spatial canopy uniformity; use multi-zone observations or CFD with blind validation.
Temperature-uniformity tests without an operating dehumidifier do not establish condensation safety.
Do not infer cavern thermal benefit from rock temperature alone; measure heat flux, moisture, groundwater, conductivity, diffusivity and seasonal boundary response.
Preserve all source inconsistencies and scope warnings. Unknown values are not zero and must not be substituted with another study's metric.
